2027-08-01.title: Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost · Sunday School Day
readings: If your brother listens, you have regained him
The sun of righteousness shall rise
Do not hesitate to visit the sick
God is a God not of disorder but of peace
Jesus sends out the Twelve two by two
2027-08-01.alt: Season of Pentecost. The Fifteen Days' Fast (Shunoyo Nombu) begins today and ends on 15 August, the Assumption of Mary. Mort Shmuni, her seven sons and their teacher Eleazar; St Alphonsus Liguori. Syro-Malankara Catholic Sunday School Day: the Holy Qurbono offering and the cover collection are sent to the eparchial centres for faith formation.
2027-08-01.verse: He will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.
theo: On the day the Church gives to Sunday school, the readings speak about how faith is passed on: from person to person, from parents to children, from the apostles to the world. In the evening Gospel Jesus teaches the hardest kind of love: “If another member of the church sins against you, go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone. If the member listens to you, you have regained that one.” The aim is not to win an argument but to win back a brother. Leviticus had already joined the two commands together: “you shall reprove your neighbor… but you shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

The same Gospel gives the smallest Church its greatest promise: “where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.” A family that prays together in the evening is such a gathering. A Sunday school class of ten children and one tired teacher is such a gathering. Christ is in the midst of them.

In the Gospel of the Qurbono Jesus sends the Twelve two by two with nothing but a staff. “So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.” The Church still anoints the sick with oil in the sacrament of the Anointing. St James adds the test of every faith: “So faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.” Sirach shows what those works look like: “Do not avoid those who weep, but mourn with those who mourn. Do not hesitate to visit the sick.”

Malachi, the last of the prophets, closes the Old Testament with a promise: “for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings,” and the Lord will send Elijah, who “will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.” Today we remember a mother whose heart was wholly turned toward her children and toward God: Mort Shmuni, who encouraged her seven sons to die rather than abandon the law of God (2 Maccabees 7). The Fifteen Days' Fast begins today; with Mary, who kept all these things in her heart, let us hand on the faith to the next generation.
conn: Malachi 4:5–6 is the last word of the prophets. The angel Gabriel quotes it about John the Baptist: he will go “with the spirit and power of Elijah… to turn the hearts of parents to their children” (Luke 1:17).
Leviticus 19:17–18 and Matthew 18:15: to correct a brother in private is a form of love, not of hatred.
Mark 6:13 and James 5:14: the apostles anointed the sick; the Church sees here a sign of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.

The mother of the seven Maccabean martyrs is called Shmuni in the Syriac tradition. Her sons and the old scribe Eleazar (2 Maccabees 6–7) are honoured together on 1 August, the first day of the Fifteen Days' Fast.
altar: “Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.” At the Holy Qurbono the whole parish, children and teachers, parents and grandparents, gathers in his name, and he is present not only among us but on the altar, given for us. From here we go out, like the Twelve, to heal and to teach.

Preaching on the mother of the Maccabees, he praised her as a mother who gave birth to her sons twice: once to this life, and again, by her encouragement, to eternal life (Homilies on the Maccabees).
magis: Parents are the first educators of their children in the faith; the family is a domestic church.
“Faith apart from works is dead”; charity demands beneficence and fraternal correction.
Family catechesis precedes, accompanies and enriches all other forms of catechesis.
saints: 1 August: Mort Shmuni, her seven sons and Eleazar; St Alphonsus Liguori; the Fifteen Days' Fast begins. 4 August: St John Mary Vianney. 5 August: anniversary of the Eparchy of Parassala (2017). 6 August (Fri): the Transfiguration of Our Lord.
2027-08-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, you promised to be among us when we gather in your name. Bless our Sunday school teachers and children, our parents and grandparents. Turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents. Give us courage to correct in love, a faith that works, and hearts that visit the sick and weep with those who weep. Through the prayers of Mary, whose Assumption we await in this fast, and of Mort Shmuni and her sons. Amen.

illus: A grandmother in Kerala could not read well, but every evening she sat on the veranda with her grandchildren and the rosary. Years later one of them, now an engineer in Germany, said at her funeral: “I learned the faith in Sunday school, but I learned to love God on her veranda.”

kidsaint: Mort Shmuni and her seven sons (1 August)

In the time of the Maccabees a cruel king tried to force the Jews to break God's law. A mother and her seven sons refused. One by one the sons were killed, and the mother encouraged each of them to stay faithful to God, because God would raise them up. The Syriac tradition calls her Shmuni. Lesson: a brave mother can teach her children to love God more than anything.
term: The Fifteen Days' Fast, from 1 to 15 August, in preparation for the feast of the Assumption (Shunoyo, the “passing” of Mary). The faithful fast, pray and give alms with Mary.
termMore: The parish school of faith formation for children, held on Sundays around the Holy Qurbono. On Sunday School Day the offering supports catechesis in the eparchy.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Sunday School Day. Who first taught you to make the sign of the cross? A mother, a grandmother, a Sunday school teacher in a small classroom? Faith is not downloaded; it is handed on, person to person, heart to heart. The last prophet, Malachi, promised that God would “turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.” That is what every good home and every good Sunday school does.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches us to correct one another with love: go to your brother alone, point out the fault, and if he listens, “you have regained that one.” Not to shame him, but to win him back. Teachers do this every week with patience. Parents do it every day. And Jesus adds a promise: “where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.” A family praying at night is a little Church.

Jesus sent the Twelve two by two. They preached repentance, cast out demons and anointed the sick with oil. St James says faith without works is dead. Sirach says: do not avoid those who weep; do not hesitate to visit the sick. Our children learn the faith not only from what we say but from what they see us do.

Today the Fifteen Days' Fast begins, and we remember Mort Shmuni, the mother of seven sons who chose God above everything. Let us thank our catechists, support the Sunday school generously, and pray together as families every evening of this fast, with Mary, the Mother of God. Amen.
kids: Children, today is your day: Sunday School Day! Thank your teachers, who give their Sundays to teach you about Jesus.
Jesus said: when two or three pray together in my name, I am with them. When you pray with your family at night, Jesus is right there.
Today a fast of fifteen days begins, before Mary's feast. Can you say one Hail Mary every day for your teacher?

intro: Theme: “He will turn the hearts of parents to their children.”
Sunday School Day: faith is handed on person to person, through loving correction, prayer together and works of mercy. The Fifteen Days' Fast begins.

sub: Correction is an act of love, not of victory.
Go alone first; the aim is to win back a brother.
Leviticus joins reproof and love together.
q: You shall not hate in your heart anyone of your kin; you shall reprove your neighbor, or you will incur guilt yourself. You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
If another member of the church sins against you, go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone. If the member listens to you, you have regained that one.
points.apply: Is there someone you need to speak to gently and privately? Pray, then go.

points.h: Two or three in my name
sub: The smallest gathering in Christ's name has his presence.
A family praying at night is a little Church.
A Sunday school class is such a gathering too.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.
points.apply: Gather as a family each evening of the fast for a short prayer.

sub: Sirach shows the works: weep with those who weep, visit the sick.
The Twelve anointed the sick; the Church still does in the sacrament of Anointing.
q: Do not avoid those who weep, but mourn with those who mourn. Do not hesitate to visit the sick, because for such deeds you will be loved.
So faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.
points.apply: Visit one sick or grieving person during the Fifteen Days' Fast.
